domains.title: Ball Mastery
domains.description: Secure, adaptable control under realistic pressure.

domains.title: Receiving & First Touch
domains.description: Receive to protect, connect, or progress.

domains.title: Passing & Combination Play
domains.description: Connect accurately and combine to move opponents.

domains.title: Scanning & Decision-Making
domains.description: Gather useful information and choose effective actions.

domains.title: Support, Width & Depth
domains.description: Create useful team spacing around the ball.

domains.title: 1v1 Attacking
domains.description: Unbalance and beat defenders with purpose.

domains.title: 1v1 Defending
domains.description: Delay, direct, and regain without diving in.

domains.title: Creating & Finishing Chances
domains.description: Create, attack, and finish high-value opportunities.

domains.title: Team Defending
domains.description: Protect central space and regain together.

domains.title: Transition to Attack
domains.description: Recognize and exploit the moment after regaining.

domains.title: Transition to Defense
domains.description: React together immediately after losing possession.

domains.title: Goalkeeping
domains.description: Develop safe technique, positioning, and distribution.

domains.title: Communication & Leadership
domains.description: Share timely information and help teammates organize.

domains.title: Reflection & Game Understanding
domains.description: Explain decisions, learn from evidence, and transfer learning.

blocks.title: Block 1 · Ball mastery and first touch
blocks.description: Secure the ball, receive with purpose, scan early, and communicate useful information.

blocks.title: Block 2 · Passing and support
blocks.description: Connect with useful weight, create support angles, and solve early 1v1 pictures.

blocks.title: Block 3 · Width, depth, and buildup
blocks.description: Build from the goalkeeper, stretch with width and depth, and progress through or around the first press.

blocks.title: Block 4 · Combination play and finishing
blocks.description: Combine to create chances, finish under realistic pressure, and exploit transition advantages.

blocks.title: Block 5 · Transition and team defending
blocks.description: Defend 1v1 with control, protect central space, and react immediately after loss.

blocks.title: Block 6 · Leadership, reflection, and transfer
blocks.description: Integrate prior goals, organize teammates, and convert film evidence into transferable next actions.

goals.title: Control Across Surfaces
goals.description: Use both feet and varied surfaces to keep the ball available while moving.
principles: Keep the ball within the next-action distance.
Use the surface that protects the intended route.
observableIndicators: Carries with inside, outside, and sole on both feet.
Changes surface without breaking stride.
Keeps the ball playable while looking beyond it.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Single-surface dependence
commonFailurePatterns.description: Uses one foot or surface until pressure closes the route.

coachFeedbackExamples: Your outside touch opened the lane; now check over your shoulder.
Try the same route with your other foot and keep the ball one step away.

goals.title: Change Speed and Direction
goals.description: Use controlled turns and acceleration to escape pressure or enter space.
principles: Slow to invite pressure, then accelerate away.
Turn into visible space rather than by habit.
observableIndicators: Decelerates before a controlled change of direction.
Takes the exit touch beyond the defender's reach.
Accelerates for at least three steps after turning.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Turn without escape
commonFailurePatterns.description: Completes a move but leaves the ball close enough for an immediate second challenge.

coachFeedbackExamples: The turn worked; make your exit touch longer so you actually escape.
You saw the space early—change pace after the cut to use it.

goals.title: Shield and Retain
goals.description: Use body position and legal contact to protect possession until support arrives.
principles: Place the body between opponent and ball.
Retain with a purpose: escape, pass, or draw support.
coachCues: Feel pressure; move the ball away.
observableIndicators: Adopts a balanced side-on stance before contact.
Uses the far foot to keep the ball away from pressure.
Exits or releases once a safe option appears.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Static shielding
commonFailurePatterns.description: Stops over the ball and remains trapped instead of adjusting feet or finding an exit.

coachFeedbackExamples: Good body position; keep moving your feet so the defender cannot reach around.
You protected it—now release as soon as your teammate gives an angle.

goals.title: Escape Double Pressure
goals.description: Recognize a second defender and protect, combine, or change direction before being trapped.
principles: A second defender creates space elsewhere.
Escape before both defenders close the same side.
observableIndicators: Scans for the covering defender before the first duel.
Changes route or releases before the trap closes.
Finds the teammate or space vacated by double pressure.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Dribbling into the trap
commonFailurePatterns.description: Focuses on beating the first defender and carries directly into cover.

coachFeedbackExamples: You beat one, but the second was waiting—scan before your move.
Two defenders came to you; the early pass would free a teammate.

goals.title: Receive with an Open Body
goals.description: Prepare a side-on shape that keeps forward and safe options visible.
principles: Arrive where hips can see two directions.
Prepare before the ball arrives.
observableIndicators: Checks shoulder before setting body shape.
Receives side-on when pressure allows.
Can play forward or retain with the next action.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Closed reception
commonFailurePatterns.description: Faces the passer with feet square and needs extra touches to turn.

coachFeedbackExamples: Your shoulder check was early; now let your hips face the next space.
Open one more step so your first touch can travel forward.

goals.title: First Touch Away from Pressure
goals.description: Direct the first touch away from the nearest challenge while preserving the next option.
principles: First touch solves the immediate pressure.
Touch toward a useful next action, not merely away.
observableIndicators: Identifies the pressure side before contact.
Uses the foot farther from the defender when appropriate.
Completes the next action before pressure recovers.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Touch into pressure
commonFailurePatterns.description: Receives with the near foot and leaves the ball on the defender's side.

coachFeedbackExamples: You felt the defender; use your far foot to take the ball across.
That touch escaped pressure—make the next pass while the gap is open.

goals.title: Receive Between Lines
goals.description: Find and use pockets between opponents' units without blocking a teammate's lane.
principles: Move out of cover shadows before the pass.
Receive where the next line can be threatened.
observableIndicators: Adjusts position to become visible through a passing window.
Checks behind before the pass enters.
Turns, sets, or bounces the ball according to pressure.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Hidden in cover
commonFailurePatterns.description: Waits directly behind an opponent and asks for an unavailable pass.

coachFeedbackExamples: Slide two steps out of the defender's shadow before asking.
You found the pocket; your scan tells you whether to turn or set.

goals.title: Receive an Aerial Ball
goals.description: Cushion a dropping ball safely into controllable space using an appropriate surface.
principles: Get in line with the flight early.
Cushion rather than rebound.
observableIndicators: Moves feet to align with the ball's flight.
Selects foot, thigh, or chest appropriately.
Brings the ball within playing distance in no more than two contacts.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Rigid first contact
commonFailurePatterns.description: Meets the ball with a stiff surface and loses it beyond immediate reach.

coachFeedbackExamples: You tracked it well; relax the surface as the ball arrives.
Choose the thigh here so the ball drops in front of your next step.

goals.title: Pass with Useful Weight
goals.description: Deliver accurate ground passes at a speed the receiver can use immediately.
principles: Weight serves the receiver's next action.
Accuracy includes the correct foot and side.
observableIndicators: Passes arrive within the receiver's controllable stride.
Adjusts speed for distance and pressure.
Targets the receiver's safe or forward foot intentionally.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Playable but unhelpful pass
commonFailurePatterns.description: Reaches the teammate but forces them toward pressure or to stop moving.

coachFeedbackExamples: It reached your teammate; aim for the far foot so they can play forward.
Add weight across that distance so the defender cannot intercept.

goals.title: Use a Wall Pass
goals.description: Combine around a defender with timed support, a set pass, and movement beyond.
principles: Pass and move immediately.
The return pass meets the runner beyond pressure.
coachCues: One touch if the picture is clear.
observableIndicators: First passer accelerates after releasing the ball.
Supporting player angles the return beyond the defender.
Pair completes the combination without occupying the same lane.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Pass and admire
commonFailurePatterns.description: First passer remains stationary, removing the return option.

coachFeedbackExamples: Your first pass drew the defender; sprint beyond for the return.
Angle the set pass into your teammate's path, not back under pressure.

goals.title: Connect the Third Player
goals.description: Use a set or bounce pass to release a teammate facing forward.
principles: The first receiver can connect rather than turn.
Third-player movement begins before the set pass.
observableIndicators: Third player adjusts into a visible forward-facing lane.
Middle player sets with controlled weight.
Combination bypasses at least one opponent line.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Late third-player movement
commonFailurePatterns.description: The next receiver waits until the set pass is made and the lane closes.

coachFeedbackExamples: Move as the first pass travels so you arrive facing forward.
Your set was clean; place it away from the marker for the third player.

goals.title: Switch the Point of Attack
goals.description: Move the ball away from congestion to exploit width on the opposite side.
principles: Circulate before forcing through a crowded lane.
The far side prepares before the switch arrives.
coachCues: Secure first pass, speed the next.
observableIndicators: Recognizes when the ball side is overloaded.
Uses one or more secure passes to access the far side.
Far-side player holds useful width and receives facing forward.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Forced direct switch
commonFailurePatterns.description: Attempts a long risky ball through pressure when a secure connecting pass is available.

coachFeedbackExamples: You saw the far side; use the central connector to make the switch safer.
Stay wide one more second so the switch creates room to advance.

goals.title: Scan Before Receiving
goals.description: Check relevant spaces before the pass arrives to locate pressure and options.
principles: Scan while the ball travels elsewhere.
Look for information that changes the next action.
observableIndicators: Looks away from the ball at least once before receiving.
Can identify pressure side through subsequent action or explanation.
Body shape reflects information gathered.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Empty head turn
commonFailurePatterns.description: Glances without changing position, body shape, or next action despite visible pressure.

coachFeedbackExamples: You checked; now use what you saw and receive away from that defender.
Scan earlier while the passer is preparing, not as the ball reaches you.

goals.title: Scan Beyond the Next Action
goals.description: Notice the next teammate, defender, or space before making the current pass.
principles: See one action ahead without predetermining.
Use the next picture to improve the current pass.
observableIndicators: Checks the area beyond the intended receiver.
Pass choice helps the receiver's likely next action.
Moves after passing based on the developing picture.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Single-action focus
commonFailurePatterns.description: Completes a pass then reacts late because the next pressure or option was not observed.

coachFeedbackExamples: Before you play, look beyond your teammate to see their pressure.
That forward-foot pass showed you had already seen the next lane.

goals.title: Choose Progress or Retention
goals.description: Distinguish when to advance, combine, or secure possession in 9v9 play.
principles: Progress when advantage is present.
Retention can create a better forward moment.
coachCues: Can we go? Must we keep?
Forward with advantage, secure without it.
observableIndicators: Attempts forward play when a receiver has time or space.
Uses a secure option when forward lanes are controlled.
Reassesses after each pass rather than repeating one choice.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Forward at any cost
commonFailurePatterns.description: Forces a vertical action despite a compact opponent and available support.

coachFeedbackExamples: Forward was blocked; your reset can move them before we try again.
That was the moment to go—the receiver had space behind their midfield.

goals.title: Recognize Overload or Isolation
goals.description: Identify whether to combine around numbers or attack an isolated defender.
principles: Use extra teammates to combine through pressure.
Use space to attack a favorable isolated duel.
observableIndicators: Identifies a local numerical advantage before acting.
Chooses combination play in crowded overloads.
Finds or uses an isolated 1v1 when cover is distant.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Wrong solution for the picture
commonFailurePatterns.description: Dribbles into an overload or passes away from a favorable isolated duel.

coachFeedbackExamples: Three of us are around two defenders—combine before carrying.
Their fullback has no cover; receive and attack that space.

goals.title: Create a Support Angle
goals.description: Offer a visible passing lane at a distance suited to pressure and the next action.
principles: Move off the defender's line.
Distance changes with pressure and pass speed.
observableIndicators: Moves out of a defender's cover shadow.
Adjusts closer under pressure and farther when space permits.
Receives with at least two next-action options.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Flat support
commonFailurePatterns.description: Stands directly beside or behind the ball carrier, allowing one defender to cover both.

coachFeedbackExamples: Drop at an angle so the defender cannot screen both of you.
The ball carrier is pressed—come close enough for a safe release.

goals.title: Use Full Team Width
goals.description: Stretch the 9v9 field responsibly to open central and wide passing lanes.
principles: Width enlarges gaps between defenders.
Wide players reconnect when the ball or game phase changes.
observableIndicators: Wide players occupy separate outside channels in possession.
Width opens a visible central lane for a teammate.
Far-side player adjusts inward when balance or transition risk requires it.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Width without connection
commonFailurePatterns.description: Stays on the touchline when the ball is far away and cannot support or recover.

coachFeedbackExamples: Hold the line while we build; your width is opening the middle.
Now slide in a channel so you can connect and protect the far side.

goals.title: Provide Penetrating Depth
goals.description: Threaten space beyond the back line while remaining connected to buildup.
principles: Depth stretches defenders away from the ball.
Runs are timed to the passer's ability to play.
coachCues: Go when the passer can see you.
observableIndicators: At least one attacker threatens behind during settled possession.
Runner checks line and passer before accelerating.
Deep player reconnects when a penetrating pass is unavailable.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Disconnected depth
commonFailurePatterns.description: Stays beyond useful passing range or runs while the passer is under closed pressure.

coachFeedbackExamples: Your depth pinned the defender; check back when the passer cannot play forward.
Wait until your teammate lifts their head, then accelerate beyond.

goals.title: Balance Behind the Ball
goals.description: Maintain connected cover behind attacks so possession can recycle and transitions can be defended.
principles: Attack with protection behind the ball.
Supporting depth shifts as the ball travels.
observableIndicators: One or more players remain available behind the ball.
Balancing players shift toward the active side without crowding it.
A backward pass can be received facing the field.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Everyone ahead
commonFailurePatterns.description: All nearby players run beyond the ball, removing both the reset and transition cover.

coachFeedbackExamples: Hold behind this attack so we can reset or stop the counter.
Shift across with the ball, but keep enough distance to see the field.

goals.title: Attack the Defender's Front Foot
goals.description: Approach under control and move as the defender shifts weight.
principles: Close space before performing the move.
Exploit the defender's weight transfer.
observableIndicators: Dribbles close enough to engage the defender.
Uses body or ball disguise before changing route.
Accelerates past the defender's shoulder after the move.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Move from too far away
commonFailurePatterns.description: Performs a skill before engaging the defender, allowing easy recovery.

coachFeedbackExamples: Carry closer before the move so the defender has to commit.
You shifted their weight—explode past the opposite shoulder.

goals.title: Protect After Beating
goals.description: Place the body and next touch between the recovering defender and the ball.
principles: Winning the first step is not the end of the duel.
The exit line protects the ball from recovery.
coachCues: First step wins; next touch protects.
observableIndicators: Exit touch crosses or clears the defender's recovery path.
Uses arm and torso legally to protect space.
Maintains speed into the next action.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Re-entry into the duel
commonFailurePatterns.description: Cuts back into the beaten defender's recovery path without a tactical reason.

coachFeedbackExamples: You beat them; now drive across their line to stay in front.
Keep the next touch on your far foot while they recover.

goals.title: Isolate a Wide Defender
goals.description: Use width, timing, and teammate movement to create space for a wide 1v1.
principles: Clear nearby space before the duel.
Attack while cover is too far to help.
observableIndicators: Nearby teammate moves away from the intended duel lane.
Attacker receives with room to face forward.
Attacker initiates before a second defender arrives.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Crowded isolation
commonFailurePatterns.description: A teammate moves into the same lane and brings an extra defender to the duel.

coachFeedbackExamples: Clear inside so the wide player has one defender, not two.
You are isolated now—attack before their midfielder recovers.

goals.title: Choose Dribble or Pass
goals.description: Read pressure, cover, and teammate advantage before entering a 1v1.
principles: Dribble to create advantage, not to prove skill.
Release when a defender commits and frees a teammate.
observableIndicators: Attacks when the defender is isolated and space exists.
Passes when cover closes the dribbling route.
Releases to a teammate after drawing an extra defender.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Automatic dribble
commonFailurePatterns.description: Carries into every defender regardless of cover or a teammate's better position.

coachFeedbackExamples: The defender was alone—that was your moment to attack.
You drew the second defender; release now to use the teammate you freed.

goals.title: Delay and Show
goals.description: Approach under control, block the dangerous route, and guide the attacker toward help.
principles: Protect the most dangerous space first.
Delay until support improves the duel.
observableIndicators: Closes space quickly then shortens steps.
Adopts a balanced side-on stance.
Guides the attacker away from central danger.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Straight-line dive
commonFailurePatterns.description: Continues at full speed into the tackle and is beaten by one touch.

coachFeedbackExamples: Your approach was quick; brake earlier so you can react.
Angle your run to close the middle and show them toward support.

goals.title: Defend the Ball Side
goals.description: Adjust feet and distance to prevent the attacker crossing the defender's front.
principles: Stay between ball and protected space.
Move feet before reaching.
observableIndicators: Maintains a distance that permits reaction.
Adjusts laterally without crossing feet unnecessarily.
Uses body position to block the direct route.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Reaching from behind
commonFailurePatterns.description: Lets the attacker cross the body line, then relies on a trailing tackle.

coachFeedbackExamples: Move your feet across first; do not reach from the wrong side.
Stay half a step farther away so you can match the next touch.

goals.title: Time the Defensive Challenge
goals.description: Win or poke the ball when the attacker's touch separates from control.
principles: Patience creates a clearer tackling moment.
Challenge through the ball with balance.
observableIndicators: Delays while touches remain protected.
Steps in as the ball moves beyond the attacker's stride.
Attempts to retain or direct the regained ball safely.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Challenge on a protected ball
commonFailurePatterns.description: Tackles while the attacker has full control and exposes space behind.

coachFeedbackExamples: Keep delaying until their touch leaves their foot.
Good win—take the next touch away from the recovering attacker.

goals.title: Recover Goal Side
goals.description: Sprint along an efficient line to protect central space and rejoin the defensive unit.
principles: First recovery steps are urgent.
Recover toward danger, not merely toward the ball.
observableIndicators: Transitions immediately into a recovery sprint.
Uses an inside line that protects the route to goal.
Slows into a controllable defending position near the play.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Chasing directly behind
commonFailurePatterns.description: Runs only toward the ball and leaves a central passing or running lane open.

coachFeedbackExamples: Take the inside route first so you protect goal while recovering.
Sprint now, then arrive under control when you can affect the play.

goals.title: Form a Buildup Starting Shape
goals.description: Create clear goalkeeper, defender, and midfielder lines for a 9v9 restart.
principles: Stretch the first press vertically and horizontally.
Keep a secure connection behind and ahead of the ball.
observableIndicators: Defenders separate to provide distinct first-pass options.
A midfielder offers beyond or beside the first pressure line.
Players avoid standing in the same passing lane.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Flat crowded start
commonFailurePatterns.description: Receivers cluster on one horizontal line and are screened together.

coachFeedbackExamples: Create a second line so one defender cannot cover both options.
Stay wide enough to stretch them, but connected enough to receive.

goals.title: Play Around the First Press
goals.description: Use goalkeeper and back-line connections to find the free side of an opponent's press.
principles: Invite pressure without trapping the receiver.
Move the ball faster than the press shifts.
coachCues: Draw one, find the free side.
Back if needed, across when open.
observableIndicators: Identifies which first-line receiver is unmarked.
Uses the goalkeeper or central defender to change sides.
Next receiver receives with time to advance or connect.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Same-side repetition
commonFailurePatterns.description: Returns repeatedly into the pressed channel without checking the free side.

coachFeedbackExamples: They sent two to one side; use the goalkeeper to reach the free defender.
Let the press travel, then move the ball across before it resets.

goals.title: Play Through the First Press
goals.description: Find a prepared midfielder between or beyond pressing players when the central lane is genuinely open.
principles: Central progression requires a visible lane and prepared receiver.
Support the receiver before the pass is played.
observableIndicators: Midfielder moves outside a cover shadow before receiving.
Pass enters only when the lane is unobstructed.
Nearby players provide a bounce or forward option for the receiver.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Forced central entry
commonFailurePatterns.description: Passes through a screened lane to a receiver facing immediate pressure without support.

coachFeedbackExamples: The midfielder is marked behind the striker—move the ball before forcing it in.
The lane is open and they checked; play firmly to the safe foot.

goals.title: Exit Buildup Pressure
goals.description: Recognize when a direct pass into a prepared target or channel is safer than short circulation.
principles: Short buildup is a tool, not a rule.
A direct exit needs an organized first and second action.
observableIndicators: Recognizes when short options are locked by equal or greater pressure.
Directs the pass toward a prepared player or usable channel.
Team compresses around the likely next contest.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Aimless clearance
commonFailurePatterns.description: Kicks long without a target, channel, or nearby support plan.

coachFeedbackExamples: Short is closed; name the target and organize around the next ball.
That direct pass had purpose—now squeeze up to support the receiver.

goals.title: Create a Cutback Lane
goals.description: Reach an advanced wide area and find a trailing teammate away from the goal line.
principles: Penetrate wide before selecting the final pass.
Arrivals occupy different finishing lines.
observableIndicators: Wide attacker reaches a position beside or behind the defensive line.
Ball carrier looks away from the crowded goalmouth toward a trailing option.
Attackers occupy separated near, central, and edge zones.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Everyone on the goal line
commonFailurePatterns.description: All attackers run beyond the ball, leaving no cutback receiver.

coachFeedbackExamples: One runner hold near the edge so the cutback has a target.
You reached the end line—look back before forcing across goal.

goals.title: Time Penalty-Area Runs
goals.description: Arrive into finishing spaces as the final passer gains control and vision.
principles: Arrive rather than wait in finishing space.
Different runs threaten different defenders.
observableIndicators: Runner checks the passer before accelerating.
At least two runners use different lanes or heights.
Runner remains available when the final ball is delivered.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Early static arrival
commonFailurePatterns.description: Enters the box too soon and stands marked before the passer can deliver.

coachFeedbackExamples: Hold outside one more step, then arrive as the passer looks up.
Split your runs—one near, one central—instead of following each other.

goals.title: Finish First Time
goals.description: Select a controlled one-contact finish when ball speed, angle, and pressure favor it.
principles: Prepare feet before the final pass arrives.
Accuracy and early contact often beat power.
observableIndicators: Scans goal and goalkeeper before contact.
Adjusts stride to meet the ball without an extra touch.
Uses an appropriate surface to direct the shot on target.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Unnecessary settling touch
commonFailurePatterns.description: Takes an extra touch that allows a defender or goalkeeper to close.

coachFeedbackExamples: You had the picture early—adjust your feet and finish without settling.
Guide this one across goal; you do not need maximum power.

goals.title: Finish Under Pressure
goals.description: Protect the shooting line and choose placement, power, or an extra touch as pressure closes.
principles: Keep the body between recovering pressure and ball.
Finish based on goalkeeper position and available time.
coachCues: Early if open; touch if needed.
observableIndicators: Uses the far foot or body line to protect the ball.
Shoots early when the goalkeeper is exposed.
Takes a purposeful setup touch when the first-time finish is blocked.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Same finish every time
commonFailurePatterns.description: Uses power or an extra touch regardless of angle, goalkeeper, and pressure.

coachFeedbackExamples: The defender is recovering on your right—keep it on your left to strike.
The goalkeeper is set; your extra touch can create a new angle.

goals.title: Protect Central Space
goals.description: Prioritize the route to goal and force possession toward less dangerous areas.
principles: Central danger is protected before wide access.
Pressure and cover share the same defensive picture.
observableIndicators: Nearest defender angles pressure away from goal.
Covering players remain inside likely central receivers.
Unit shifts without opening a direct central lane.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Chasing the touchline
commonFailurePatterns.description: Multiple defenders leave central space to pressure one wide player.

coachFeedbackExamples: One presses wide; the rest protect inside options.
Your angle must remove the route toward goal before you close the ball.

goals.title: Coordinate Pressure, Cover, Balance
goals.description: Organize first, second, and far-side defenders around the ball.
principles: Pressure needs immediate cover.
Far-side balance protects switches and runners.
observableIndicators: Nearest defender applies controlled pressure.
Second defender provides angled cover at a useful distance.
Far-side defender narrows while seeing ball and opponent.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Flat defensive line
commonFailurePatterns.description: Covering defenders stand level with pressure and cannot protect behind.

coachFeedbackExamples: Drop behind the presser at an angle so you can cover the inside touch.
Far side, tuck in but keep seeing your runner.

goals.title: Shift as a Connected Unit
goals.description: Move defensive lines together as the ball travels across or backward.
principles: Travel while the pass travels.
Distances between teammates remain compact enough to help.
observableIndicators: Multiple defenders shift as the ball is traveling.
Horizontal gaps remain small enough for adjacent cover.
Back and midfield lines move in the same direction.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Staggered reaction
commonFailurePatterns.description: One player presses after the pass while teammates remain on the previous side.

coachFeedbackExamples: Move while the ball travels so the receiver sees pressure on arrival.
Back line and midfield must shift together; close the gap between you.

goals.title: Defend Crosses in the Box
goals.description: Protect goal-side zones, track runners, and clear into safer areas.
principles: See ball and opponent before delivery.
First contact moves danger away from central goal.
observableIndicators: Defenders adopt positions between runners and goal.
Players scan between ball and assigned space or runner.
Clearances are directed away from the central scoring area.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Watching only the ball
commonFailurePatterns.description: Loses a runner behind while facing the crosser throughout the delivery.

coachFeedbackExamples: Open your body so you can see both the crosser and runner.
Make first contact and direct it wide, not back into the middle.

goals.title: First Look Forward After Regain
goals.description: Scan immediately for a safe forward advantage when possession changes.
principles: Transition space may disappear quickly.
Forward is preferred only when control and advantage exist.
observableIndicators: Regaining player lifts head after securing the ball.
Attempts a forward pass or carry when space is available.
Uses a safe option when the regain is unstable.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Blind forward ball
commonFailurePatterns.description: Kicks forward immediately without securing possession or identifying a target.

coachFeedbackExamples: Win it cleanly, then check forward before they recover.
No forward lane this time—secure the first pass and let us spread.

goals.title: Spread After Regain
goals.description: Expand quickly from defensive positions to provide forward, wide, and supporting options.
principles: Regain changes the team's shape immediately.
Expansion must preserve one secure connection.
observableIndicators: Wide players move away from congestion after a clean regain.
A forward option threatens space beyond.
At least one teammate stays close enough to secure possession.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Everyone runs away
commonFailurePatterns.description: All teammates sprint forward and leave the regaining player isolated.

coachFeedbackExamples: Stretch quickly, but one player stay underneath the ball.
Your wide run opened the field; keep checking whether the pass is available.

goals.title: Break a Line in Transition
goals.description: Use the first controlled actions after a regain to bypass a disorganized opponent line.
principles: Attack before defensive lines reconnect.
The line-breaking action needs support beyond it.
observableIndicators: Identifies a gap between recovering opponents.
Pass or carry moves beyond at least one defensive line.
A teammate supports the receiver's next action.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Slow sideways transition
commonFailurePatterns.description: Circulates without pressure until the opponent restores compact shape despite an open forward lane.

coachFeedbackExamples: The gap is open now—play through before their midfield recovers.
Support the receiver after the line break; do not admire the pass.

goals.title: Secure Transition When Closed
goals.description: Recognize when the quick attack is gone and establish composed possession.
principles: A transition ends when the advantage disappears.
Retention allows the team to rebuild spacing.
observableIndicators: Recognizes when opponents have recovered behind the ball.
Uses a supporting or backward pass instead of forcing play.
Team expands into a stable possession shape after the reset.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Transition forced too long
commonFailurePatterns.description: Continues a low-percentage attack after numbers and space no longer favor it.

coachFeedbackExamples: They recovered—keep the ball and rebuild our width.
The fast attack was on at first; now use the support behind you.

goals.title: React Immediately to Loss
goals.description: Change role on the first steps after possession is lost.
principles: The first reaction delays or protects.
Every nearby player takes a clear defensive action.
observableIndicators: Player changes direction within the first moments after loss.
Nearest player pressures or blocks a forward route.
Other nearby players recover into cover positions.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Pause after turnover
commonFailurePatterns.description: Shows frustration or watches the ball while opponents begin the counterattack.

coachFeedbackExamples: Your next job starts the instant we lose it—press or recover now.
Good reaction; your first three steps stopped their forward pass.

goals.title: Counterpress Near the Ball
goals.description: Use nearby numbers to close the ball and immediate exits after a controllable loss.
principles: Counterpress only when distance and numbers allow.
Pressure closes forward exits before chasing the ball.
observableIndicators: Nearest player pressures under control.
Second and third players block short forward outlets.
Group abandons the press and recovers when it is bypassed.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Solo counterpress
commonFailurePatterns.description: One player chases while teammates are too far away, opening space behind.

coachFeedbackExamples: You are close enough together—one presses and two close the exits.
You are alone here; recover instead of starting a press we cannot support.

goals.title: Protect Center After Loss
goals.description: Recover inside passing and running lanes when immediate pressure cannot win the ball.
principles: Central protection slows the counterattack.
Recovery runs track danger as well as the ball.
observableIndicators: Players away from the ball sprint toward central lanes.
Recovering player checks for an opponent running beyond.
Team forms a compact barrier between ball and goal.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Wide ball chasing
commonFailurePatterns.description: Multiple players recover toward the ball while leaving the direct central route open.

coachFeedbackExamples: Recover inside the ball first; make them play around us.
Check your shoulder while you run so you can pick up the central runner.

goals.title: Delay the Counterattack
goals.description: Manage space and time until teammates recover behind the ball.
principles: Delay can be more valuable than an immediate tackle.
Protect the most dangerous route while retreating.
observableIndicators: First defender avoids an unsupported lunge.
Uses body angle to steer play away from central goal.
Retreats at a speed that permits reaction until support arrives.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Emergency dive-in
commonFailurePatterns.description: Attempts an unlikely tackle and removes the final layer of protection.

coachFeedbackExamples: You are the last cover—delay and let teammates recover.
Keep showing outside while matching their speed; the tackle can wait.

goals.title: Set for the Shot
goals.description: Adjust angle, depth, and balanced stance as the ball enters shooting range.
principles: Position is updated as the ball moves.
A balanced set permits movement in either direction.
observableIndicators: Goalkeeper adjusts toward the ball line before the shot.
Sets with feet balanced as the shooter prepares.
Maintains a clear view around or through players.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Set too early or late
commonFailurePatterns.description: Remains fixed while the ball changes angle or is still moving when the shot is struck.

coachFeedbackExamples: Travel with the pass, then set as the shooter prepares.
Take one step off your line here to improve the angle without losing balance.

goals.title: Handle or Parry Safely
goals.description: Select a secure catch or direct the ball away from central danger.
principles: Catch when body and ball permit secure control.
Parries travel wide of goal and attackers.
observableIndicators: Gets body behind catchable shots.
Uses appropriate hand shape for ball height.
Directs unavoidable rebounds away from the central goalmouth.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Central rebound
commonFailurePatterns.description: Pushes a difficult ball back into the most dangerous finishing area.

coachFeedbackExamples: Get your chest behind that ball and bring it safely into your body.
If you cannot hold it, use strong hands to send it wide.

goals.title: Choose Goalkeeper Distribution
goals.description: Select roll, throw, pass, or purposeful longer service from teammates' positions and opponent pressure.
principles: Distribution starts the next team action.
Speed of release matches the available advantage.
coachCues: Fast if open, patient if not.
observableIndicators: Scans teammate and opponent positions before release.
Selects a technique suited to distance and pressure.
Delivers toward a teammate's useful side or a purposeful channel.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Predetermined release
commonFailurePatterns.description: Uses the same distribution regardless of pressure, distance, or teammate readiness.

coachFeedbackExamples: You saw the wide player early—roll quickly into their path.
The short side is marked; wait, shift them, then choose the safer exit.

goals.title: Give Specific Information
goals.description: Use brief, timely words that tell a teammate what they cannot easily see.
principles: Useful communication is early and specific.
Words support rather than replace player decisions.
observableIndicators: Uses a teammate's name or clear directional cue.
Communicates before the teammate's action.
Message matches visible pressure, space, or support.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Noise without information
commonFailurePatterns.description: Repeatedly shouts generic words that do not clarify pressure or options.

coachFeedbackExamples: Instead of 'go,' tell them 'turn' or 'set' before the ball arrives.
That early 'player left' helped your teammate protect the ball.

goals.title: Organize Team Restarts
goals.description: Take shared responsibility for positions, options, and readiness before play restarts.
principles: Organization begins before the ball is available.
Leadership invites clear roles, not control of every action.
observableIndicators: Players identify taker and immediate options promptly.
A teammate checks defensive balance before an attacking restart.
Players use calm, specific communication to adjust positions.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Late restart confusion
commonFailurePatterns.description: Players debate roles after the ball is ready and begin from unprepared positions.

coachFeedbackExamples: Decide the taker early, then show two clear options.
Good leadership checking who protects behind the restart.

goals.title: Lead Through Response
goals.description: Respond constructively to mistakes, goals, and difficult moments so the team can perform the next action.
principles: The next action matters more than blame.
Leaders model composure and inclusion.
observableIndicators: Uses supportive language after a teammate's error.
Returns attention to role and shape promptly.
Invites or acknowledges quieter teammates' information.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Blame spiral
commonFailurePatterns.description: Gestures or comments about a mistake while the next phase continues.

coachFeedbackExamples: Acknowledge it, then help everyone reset for the next play.
Your calm cue brought your teammate back into the game—keep it specific.

goals.title: Explain a Game Decision
goals.description: Describe the information, choice, and intended outcome behind a game action.
principles: Reflection connects what was seen to what was done.
More than one reasonable choice may exist.
observableIndicators: Names at least one relevant teammate, opponent, or space.
Connects that information to the action selected.
Identifies a plausible intended outcome without claiming certainty.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Result-only explanation
commonFailurePatterns.description: Judges the action only by success or failure without discussing the game picture.

coachFeedbackExamples: Tell me what you saw before the pass, not only where it ended.
Your choice makes sense from that pressure; what other option was available?

goals.title: Review Observable Evidence
goals.description: Use a coach-selected clip or remembered moment to identify visible actions and alternatives without inventing intent.
principles: Describe visible behavior before interpreting.
Evidence supports a next-step question, not a verdict about intent.
observableIndicators: Identifies observable position, movement, or ball action.
Separates what is visible from what the player reports thinking.
Proposes one realistic alternative for the same picture.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Assumed intent
commonFailurePatterns.description: States why a player acted as fact when the evidence only shows the action and context.

coachFeedbackExamples: We can see your body was closed; tell us what you were thinking then.
Name the visible pressure first, then suggest another action you could test.

goals.title: Set a Transfer Action
goals.description: Turn reflection into one specific, observable action to try in the next match or practice.
principles: A useful target is controllable and observable.
Review whether the action was attempted, not just whether it succeeded.
observableIndicators: States a concrete action tied to a recognizable game cue.
Target can be observed by player or coach.
After play, reflects on attempts and adjusts the target.

commonFailurePatterns.title: Vague improvement goal
commonFailurePatterns.description: Chooses an outcome such as 'play better' with no observable action or trigger.

coachFeedbackExamples: Make it observable: 'scan twice before receiving centrally.'
Review how often you tried the action, even when the pass did not work.
